chunks: (Verily we are Allah’s and verily to Him shall we return)
Then he said: Our saying 'Verily we are Allah’s' is an admission of His Majesty over us and our saying 'and verily to Him shall we return' is an admission of our being mortal.
ai.seo_question: What is the deeper theological meaning of 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un' according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) offers a profound hermeneutical distinction within the verse, interpreting 'Inna lillahi' as an affirmation of divine sovereignty (al-Mulk) and 'wa inna ilayhi raji'un' as a recognition of human mortality and return (al-Hulk). This exegesis highlights the dual nature of submission, balancing the acknowledgment of God's eternal authority with the transient reality of human existence. Such interpretation underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the spiritual and ontological dimensions of Quranic phrases beyond their literal recitation.
